newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on heavy overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on heavy overseas sales.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended lower on Thursday from New York's previous close after continuous heavy selling from local and overseas players, gold dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$349.10/60 an ounce against New York's US$350.50/351.00 close on Wednesday.

Australian producer and local professional selling pushed gold down to $348.90/349.20 per ounce, but that level triggered shortcovering in the market which pushed gold back to near $349.50 per ounce, traders said.
Gold would now likely to range-trade between $348 and $352 per ounce, traders said.

Near-term support was still seen at $348 per ounce. Physical gold buying remained healthy, but Hong Kong's kilobar shortage persisted and premiums remained at a hefty 160 U.S. cents, unchanged from last week, dealers said.
Local gold ended HK$21 lower at HK$3,226 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged at -6.00.
